original_source: SMALT benchmark transect design; Sahoo et al. (2016) 6 km transect
estimation_procedure: Selected to represent a typical 2 km coastal plain fluvial cross-section spanning multiple channel belts.
uncertainty_and_limitations: 2 km covers ~7 channel belts; real outcrop transect spans 6 km.
sensitivity_to_alternatives: Shorter domains (1 km) increase edge boundary effects; larger domains (4 km) increase runtime linearly.

original_source: Average measured outcrop cliff height in Sahoo et al. (2016)
estimation_procedure: Selected to match the average stratigraphic interval above the Axel Anderson coal datum (30-70 m across logs).
uncertainty_and_limitations: Real cliff sections vary from 38 m to 93 m in preserved height.
sensitivity_to_alternatives: Thicker columns (100 m) allow more channel storeys; thinner columns (<30 m) restrict stacking.

original_source: Channel scouring threshold in fluvial sedimentology
estimation_procedure: Truncation bound preventing unphysically thin channel scours (<1.5 m).
uncertainty_and_limitations: Channel scours in field rarely preserve under 1.5 m thickness due to stream power.
sensitivity_to_alternatives: Setting to 0.5m allows tiny scours; setting to 3.0m eliminates single-storey minor channels.

original_source: Maximum multi-storey amalgamated channel body in outcrop
estimation_procedure: Truncation bound preventing unphysically thick channels exceeding domain capacity (25 m in 50 m column).
uncertainty_and_limitations: Empirical maximum in Upstream logs is 32.0 m (L2 multi-storey body).
sensitivity_to_alternatives: Allows up to 50% domain thickness for an individual amalgamated channel complex.

estimation_procedure: Stopping rule window
uncertainty_and_limitations: Tolerance band: loop terminates once current_ntg >= (target_ntg - tolerance) = 0.37 after >=3 channels.
sensitivity_to_alternatives: Prevents runaway channel placement and infinite loops.
audit_verdict: Smaller tolerance (0.02) requires more iterations; larger tolerance (0.15) terminates prematurely.
